notes: CORRECT A CHEQUE AS MANY TIMES AS YOU NEED TO. A cheque number could previously be corrected once. A second correction was refused and you were told to use a fresh cheque — honest, because the register could only remember one earlier version, but it turned a bookkeeping correction into a cheque book problem. A cheque number now keeps its whole history: every instrument it has stood for, in order. Correct it twice, or four times, and each earlier version is still on record. WHY IT MATTERS AT MONTH END. If you have already reconciled a month and signed it off, and the correction comes afterwards, that month must still show the cheque exactly as it was written — the date on it and the amount on it — because the month's cashbook still carries the payment. The register now does, and the reconciliation still balances. Your existing cheques gain their history automatically the first time this version opens your books. WHEN THE APP CANNOT READ SOMETHING, IT SAYS SO. If a check cannot be run, the app must not carry on as though it had passed. Eight places are corrected where a failed read was quietly treated as "nothing found": the over-budget warning on a commitment was skipped rather than shown; an invoice or supplier bill already posted could be edited underneath its own entry; a stock take could book the same variances twice; a petty-cash reimbursement could print with fewer vouchers on it than its cheque paid for; correcting a payment could invite a fresh cheque for money that had already left the bank; the control-account check could report all clear when it could not read its own settings; and registering a cheque could miss the entry already using that number. Each now stops and tells you what it could not read. BEFORE YOU UPDATE: take a backup — Administration, Backup & Export, "Back up the database now". This release extends the cheque register, and a backup taken beforehand is the one that restores the earlier structure should you ever want it.
